activities.title: Opa!
activities.blurb: Andreas lets one guest a night smash a plate. Tonight he's looking at you. The whole room is looking at you.

outcomes.text: Perfect arc, perfect shatter. The table by the window stands up. Andreas wipes a single tear.
It bounces. Twice. Then breaks. The room claps out of pity, which still counts.
It shatters into the dessert case. Andreas adds the baklava to your bill. "Opa," he says, quietly.

options.label: Hand it to the birthday table
options.get: Mood, a free shot of ouzo

outcomes.text: The birthday girl smashes it like it owes her money. Her whole table adopts you. Free ouzo.
They don't speak to you, but the ouzo arrives anyway. Andreas winks. You're family now. Minor family.

activities.title: Order off the menu
activities.blurb: There's a menu, and then there's what Andreas makes for people he respects. You have to ask the right way.

outcomes.text: He disappears for twenty minutes. Comes back with lamb that makes you call your own grandmother.
"My yiayia ate standing up, in silence." He brings you bread. It's excellent bread.
Your eyes water. You don't flinch. A busboy films it. The clip does numbers in Astoria.
You make it two bites. Andreas pats your shoulder and brings yogurt like a paramedic.

activities.title: Help with the lunch rush
activities.blurb: The line is out the door and the new waiter just quit to "focus on his podcast." Andreas looks at you.

outcomes.text: Twenty-two plates, zero drops. Andreas pays you in cash and calls you "the good one."
You drop one moussaka. Just the one. It still counts against your pay.
You keep forty hungry New Yorkers calm with jokes and free pita. Somebody asks for your card.
A man in a fleece vest asks to speak to the manager. You are not the manager. It's a long hour.

activities.title: Join the circle dance
activities.blurb: The bouzouki speeds up, someone's uncle grabs your hand, and suddenly you're in a circle of forty people who all know the steps.

outcomes.text: You catch the steps by the second lap. By the fifth, you're leading. An uncle you've never met calls you his favorite.
You go left when everyone goes right. Twice. They keep you in anyway. That's Greek night.
Your clip catches the exact moment Andreas does the lift. It's on three Astoria pages by midnight.
Forty seconds of the back of someone's head. Beautiful head, though.

activities.title: Beat the arcade high score
activities.blurb: The Galaxy Gobbler cabinet upstairs has had the same initials at the top since 2019: DAD. Nobody knows whose dad.

outcomes.text: New high score. You type your initials. A small crowd forms. Somewhere, a dad feels it.
Second place. DAD remains. The machine plays a sad little song just for you.
The kid beats level six. He tells everyone you're his "manager." You accept the role.
The kid loses anyway and blames you, loudly, to his mom. Character building.

activities.title: Lola's hot seat
activities.blurb: Lola pulls up a stool, opens her notes app and says, "Three questions. Don't be boring."

options.label: Spill something real
options.get: Clout, a mention in her column

outcomes.text: Lola gasps, actually gasps. "Oh, that's going in." You're quoted, anonymously, which everyone will decode.
"That's… a story about your dentist." She closes the notes app. Gently.
"No comment, but thank you for asking." Lola stares. "You'll go far. Unfortunately."
She likes it. "Mysterious. Keep that up and they'll write about you without me."

activities.title: Candlelight story night
activities.blurb: The power's out, so Lola lit every candle in the building and declared it an event. It's honestly nicer.

options.label: Tell your worst NYC story
options.get: Clout, a room that loves you

outcomes.text: The one about the rat on the G train. The room is screaming. Someone asks if you do weddings.
You tell it well but a retired cop tops it immediately. You both get a round of applause.
An old man tells a story about Astoria in 1979 and it's the best thing you've heard all year.

activities.title: Order like a New Yorker
activities.blurb: Sal respects exactly one thing: knowing what you want and saying it fast. The line behind you is already sighing.

outcomes.text: Sal nods once. That's the highest honor in Astoria. The sandwich is in your hand in forty seconds.
You say it so fast you order two by mistake. Sal charges you for both and respects you more.
"Recommend? Buddy, it's a deli." He makes you his own lunch out of spite. It's the best thing on the street.
The guy behind you says "come ON" and the whole line agrees. Sal gives you a roll. Just a roll.

activities.title: Win over Meatball
activities.blurb: The deli cat, Meatball, sleeps on the bread. She has never once acknowledged a customer. Some say she can't.

outcomes.text: Eleven minutes. Then she walks over and sits on your foot. Sal drops a tray. "She never does that."
Meatball looks at you, yawns, and turns to face the wall. A clear message.
She takes the turkey and lets you touch her head for one second. Transactional. Like New York.
She takes the turkey and leaves. Sal: "She's smarter than you."

activities.title: Get behind the counter
activities.blurb: It's the morning rush, Sal's nephew is "stuck on the N," and there are thirty construction workers who need coffee now.

outcomes.text: Light and sweet, black, regular, regular, black. You nail every one. Sal pays you and says "not bad."
You give a guy decaf. He knows. Somehow he knows. Sal docks you a little.
Fast hands, correct change, one compliment on your energy. You might be a natural.
Someone pays in quarters. All quarters. It takes nine minutes. Sal watches the whole thing.

activities.title: Get your name on the cup
activities.blurb: Jojo spells every name wrong on purpose. Today she says she's taking requests. She's smiling, which is worrying.

outcomes.text: She writes it perfectly. Then adds "(allegedly)" underneath. The whole line reads it out loud.
"Brinleigh." That's not your name. It's nobody's name. You answer to it for the rest of the day.
You say "Duchess." Jojo calls "Duchess" across the café with total commitment. Three people ask who you are.
You say "Duchess." She writes "Dutch." A man at table four asks you about tulips for ten minutes.

activities.title: Laptop row
activities.blurb: Table four has been "taking a meeting" since Tuesday. Jojo slides you a refill and nods at it. Your move.

outcomes.text: A founder pitches an investor a calendar app for your other calendars. Lola is going to love this.
Forty minutes of "circle back" and "synergy." You learn nothing. You feel older.

options.label: Pull up a chair and pitch

outcomes.text: You pitch "Jojo's tip jar, but as an app." They take your number. Jojo takes ten percent.
They think you're the barista. You take their order. Jojo lets you keep the tip.

activities.title: Jump on the bar
activities.blurb: Jojo is frothing two pitchers at once and the line has started a group chat about her. She points at the spare apron.

outcomes.text: Twenty-six drinks, one perfect leaf in the foam. Jojo films it "for film school" and pays you out of the tip jar.
You steam the oat milk until it screams. So does a customer. Jojo still pays you, with a look.
"Large cold brew for… Sir Latte?" The line cracks up and the tips go up. Jojo calls you "a natural liar."
You call "Kevin" eleven times. There are four Kevins. None of them is the right Kevin.

activities.title: Share a table
activities.blurb: The only free seat is across from a stranger with a wet umbrella and a very long story. Jojo raises an eyebrow.

outcomes.text: Her ex dated a guy who works the door at Velvet Static. You leave with a name, a tip and her number.
It's forty minutes about her umbrella. It's a very good umbrella. She shows you the receipt.
The table behind you breaks up and gets back together before the rain stops. You heard every word.
She taps you to ask what you're listening to. Nothing. You're listening to nothing. She knows.

activities.title: Get Mags's attention
activities.blurb: Forty people are waving cards at the bar. Mags has looked at none of them. There's an art to this.

options.label: Stand still and make eye contact

outcomes.text: You don't wave. You don't shout. Mags serves you first and says "finally, a professional."
Six minutes of eye contact. She serves the guy next to you. He tips her in autographs.
Mags takes the tip, makes your drink and says "Rough day? Same." Worth every coin.
She takes the tip, nods, and serves you in the exact order she was going to anyway. Fair, honestly.

activities.title: Step into the circle
activities.blurb: The DJ just dropped the song. A circle opens in the middle of the floor and nobody's brave enough to go in.

options.label: Take the center
options.cost: 10 Energy, the risk of a circle

outcomes.text: You hit every beat. The circle roars. Someone films from the balcony and Mags swings a light your way.
You slip on a glow stick, recover into a spin and act like it was choreography. Half the room believes you.
You step in. The DJ changes the song mid-move. You commit anyway. The room respects it, sort of.
You dance like nobody's watching. Nobody is. It's the best twenty minutes of your week.
A theater kid joins you and turns it into a duet. You're in their group chat now.

activities.title: The eleven-minute light
activities.blurb: For eleven minutes the sun hits the brick just right. Everyone in the room knows it. There's a line to stand in it.

options.label: Wait in line for the light

outcomes.text: Your turn lands at minute ten. Perfect light. The photo does better than your last six posts combined.
The sun goes behind a cloud the second it's your turn. You get a lovely photo of a cloud.
Nine strangers in the good light, nine tags crediting you. Mags asks for one too. That's the real honor.
Eight of the nine ask you to "try one more from lower." You end up lying on the floor of a club.

activities.title: Barback for Mags
activities.blurb: Ice, glasses, more ice. Mags hands you an apron and one rule: never, ever touch her bottle opener.

outcomes.text: Nine buckets of ice up two flights. Mags pays you and pours you something with a tiny umbrella in it.
You drop a tray of glasses in the DJ's quiet bit. The whole club cheers. Mags docks you, smiling.
Two hundred people, one long line, jokes the whole way. A guy offers you a job at his startup. You pass.
A man asks "do you know who I am?" You don't. Nobody does. It takes an hour to find out.

activities.title: Sit with Gus
activities.blurb: Gus has had the same bench since 1968. He pats the seat beside him. "Want to hear about 1987?"

outcomes.text: 1987: a blackout, a borrowed accordion and a wedding on this lawn. Best story you've heard all year.
The story about 1987 turns into a story about 1974, then a recipe. You leave with the recipe.

options.label: Challenge him to backgammon
options.get: Clout if you win, his respect

outcomes.text: You win. Gus stares at the board for a full minute, then shakes your hand. "Rematch. Tomorrow. Same bench."
Gus wins in four minutes and rates your form out loud, like a jogger's. "Good effort. Terrible strategy."

activities.title: Walk Sir Barksley
activities.blurb: Dmitri needs a coffee. Sir Barksley, the billionaire's depressed Pomeranian, needs someone who won't mention Miami.

options.label: Take him along the river
options.get: Mood, a tip from his allowance

outcomes.text: He trots. Actually trots. Dmitri nearly drops his coffee: "He hasn't trotted since the divorce." Big tip.
He sits at the first tree and won't move. You stand there together for twenty minutes. It's kind of nice.
A pigeon looks at him. He looks at you. You carry him back. Dmitri says that counts.
You tell him moving on is a process. He licks your hand. Dmitri reports it to the owner, who follows you.
You mention boats. He hears "yacht." He lies down facing the river. Dmitri sighs: "We don't say that word."

activities.title: Get past the swim-cap lady
activities.blurb: Cap, lock, no cutoffs. She once turned away a city councilman. Right now she's looking directly at your head.

options.label: Buy a cap from the machine

outcomes.text: Twelve laps in a neon cap. A 70-year-old laps you twice and gives you a thumbs-up. You'll take it.
The cap is a child's size. You swim anyway, looking like a highlighter. Nobody will ever forget you.

options.label: Say your cap is "invisible"
options.get: Entry, if she's in a mood

outcomes.text: She laughs. Actually laughs. "Okay, comedian. Today only." The lifeguards are stunned.
"Invisible cap, invisible swim." She points at the gate. A kid behind you says "oof."

activities.title: Run through the sprinklers
activities.blurb: Kids, dogs and a man in a full suit on his lunch break. Gus watches from the bench, scoring everyone's form.

outcomes.text: Gus holds up a napkin with a 9 on it. The man in the suit gives you a 7. You'll frame both.
You slip, slide four feet and stand up like you meant it. The kids give it a 10. Gus gives it a 4.

options.label: Sit at the edge with the dogs

outcomes.text: Six wet dogs decide you're their dock. Sir Barksley watches from the shade. He almost looks interested.
A doodle shakes itself dry directly onto you. Your phone is fine. Your outfit has notes.

activities.title: Fold it like a local
activities.blurb: Arben watches every new customer's first bite. A fork and he's sad all afternoon. A fold and you're family.

options.label: Fold it down the middle
options.cost: C$6, the roof of your mouth

outcomes.text: Clean fold, no drip, a bite like you've done it ten thousand times. Arben nods once. "Say less."
The fold holds. The grease doesn't. Your shirt now has a map of Queens on it.

options.label: Ask for a fork, for science

outcomes.text: Arben hands you a napkin and says "that's the fork." The line applauds him. Somebody posts it.
He gives you a fork. Silently. He doesn't speak again until closing. You feel it in your soul.

activities.title: Argue about the sign
activities.blurb: The sign says a dollar. A slice is three. Arben says it's a dollar "spiritually." Want to take this up with him?

outcomes.text: You argue so well he charges you one dollar, "for the effort." Never again, he says, smiling.
Arben argues back for twenty minutes, mostly about 2009. You pay full price and learn a lot about 2009.
"Finally, somebody who gets it." He gives you the corner slice. The corner slice is a privilege.
He narrows his eyes. "You're being sarcastic." You were. He charges you for the soda too.

activities.title: Work the counter
activities.blurb: Arben's daughter has a soccer game and his cousin has been "running late" since 2019. He tosses you an apron. "Fast hands."

outcomes.text: Crispy bottoms, every one. Arben checks a slice, says nothing, and pays you extra. That's a speech, for him.
One pie slides off the peel and lands cheese-down. Arben mourns it briefly and pays you anyway.
Two slices and a soda, two slices and a soda. You find a rhythm like a drummer. Cash and a slice.
A man pays with a coupon from 2009. It's real. Arben honors it. You lose six minutes and some faith.

activities.title: Feed the stranded
activities.blurb: A whole train's worth of people are in here, hungry and furious at the Metro Rail Authority. Arben looks at you.

options.label: Carry pies up to the platform

outcomes.text: Six pies up to the stuck platform. A whole train car applauds. A nurse calls you "a public service."
The trains start moving the second you get up there. You eat a whole pie alone on the platform. Not bad.
Twelve strangers share their worst commutes. One man has been on the N since Tuesday. You swap numbers.
Everyone talks over each other about a train none of them even takes. Arben hands out napkins.

activities.title: Take on cabinet three
activities.blurb: A twelve-year-old has held the top score on cabinet three for a month. He's here. He's watching you put in a token.

options.label: Go for the record
options.get: Clout if you beat the kid

outcomes.text: New record. The kid nods once and leaves to practice. Pixel announces it over the speakers, twice.
You reach level nine. The kid's record is level forty. He pats your shoulder on his way out.

options.label: Ask the kid for lessons
options.get: Mood, a mentor half your age

outcomes.text: He teaches you a combo and charges one soda. Pixel says you're "the first student who ever listened."
He explains for twenty minutes in words you don't know. You nod at every one of them.

activities.title: Save the honor system
activities.blurb: The energy-drink fridge runs on the honor system. The honor system is failing. Pixel needs someone who looks honest.

outcomes.text: You collect every dollar owed, plus a handwritten apology. Pixel pays you and laminates the apology.
A streamer argues with you live for nine minutes. You lose the argument. You win the chat.
"The fridge sees you, Tyler." There are four Tylers. All four pay. One cries a little.
Someone writes "no" under your sign. Then "ok fine" under that. Then pays in nickels.

activities.title: Enter the bracket
activities.blurb: Sixteen players, one stage, a crowd that boos for fun and a trophy shaped like a controller. Pixel's on the mic.

outcomes.text: You win. The whole thing. The controller trophy is heavier than it looks. Pixel gets emotional on the mic.
You make the final and lose to a guy in a cape. Still: a bracket screenshot and a lot of new followers.
Out in round one to a twelve-year-old. The crowd boos. Not you. The kid. Strange crowd.
"HE'S IN THE CORNER. HE'S STILL IN THE CORNER." You're a natural. Pixel offers you the mic every Friday.
You call the wrong player's name for an entire match. Both players' moms complain.

activities.title: Winner stays on
activities.blurb: Pixel dug out a console from 2004 and hooked it to the generator. One controller, forty gamers, winner stays on.

outcomes.text: Eleven straight wins. The room chants your name. The generator nearly gives out from the noise.
You lose your first game to a guy who's never played. Beginner's luck is real and it hates you.

options.label: Run the hype from the couch
options.get: Mood, a room that loves you

outcomes.text: You narrate every game like a nature documentary. By midnight people are requesting you by name.
You hype so hard you knock over the only lamp. Darkness. Cheering. Pixel finds a flashlight.

activities.title: Spot the narrator
activities.blurb: A man is benching a lot of weight and narrating it in full sentences. He catches your eye. "Spot me, chief?"

outcomes.text: Textbook spot. He hugs you, sweatily, and tells the whole gym you're "a real one." Coach Bogdana nods.
Rep two gets stuck. You lift it together, both shaking. It's the closest you've felt to anyone all week.

options.label: Narrate his set back to him

outcomes.text: "He's reaching deep. He's thinking about his father." The whole row laughs. He laughs hardest. New gym friend.
He doesn't laugh. He finishes the set and asks for your form notes. You do not have form notes.

activities.title: The forbidden mirror selfie
activities.blurb: Pressed Iron has the best mirror in Brooklyn and a sign: NO MIRROR SELFIES. Coach Bogdana enforces it personally.

outcomes.text: Perfect angle, perfect pump, zero witnesses. You post it as "just a normal Tuesday." It does numbers.
Coach Bogdana appears behind you in the mirror like a horror movie. Twenty burpees. Someone films them.

options.label: Ask Coach Bogdana to take it

outcomes.text: She stares. Then takes it. Then retakes it lower. "Shoulders back. Again." Best photo of you ever taken.
"Absolutely not." But she fixes your squat stance on the way past. You'll take it.

activities.title: Survive the 6 AM class
activities.blurb: Forty-five minutes, no breaks, one bucket by the door "just in case." Coach Bogdana looks at you: "New? Front row."

options.label: Take the front row
options.cost: 18 Energy, your legs for two days

outcomes.text: You finish. Front row. She says "not bad," which regulars swear she's said four times in ten years.
You make it to minute thirty and lie down. She lets you. "Rest is a choice. A wrong one."

options.label: Hide in the back row
options.cost: 18 Energy, her eyes find you anyway

outcomes.text: You hide behind a finance guy in a vest for forty minutes. It works. You leave feeling great, secretly.
"Back row. I see you." She moves you to the front, alone, facing the class. Everyone learns your name.

activities.title: Get the edge table
activities.blurb: The edge table has the whole skyline behind it. Thaddeus, the host, has a clipboard and a waitlist "into next spring."

outcomes.text: You compliment the clipboard. Specifically. He softens. The edge table is suddenly free. "A cancellation," he lies.
He smiles, writes your name down and seats you by the kitchen door. With a view. Of the kitchen.
It's literally air. But it's air with a skyline in it, and your photo looks like a magazine cover.
You get the edge table. A cloud parks on the skyline for your entire meal. Thaddeus shrugs. "Weather."

activities.title: The tiny plate
activities.blurb: The chef's signature: one perfect bite on a plate the size of a car tire. C$38. It's suspicious how good it is.

outcomes.text: Angle eleven is the one. Your post beats the restaurant's own. Thaddeus asks if they can repost it.
By angle twelve a waiter clears it. "You were finished, yes?" You were not finished.

options.label: Just eat it, like a person

outcomes.text: You eat it. You understand everything. You understand nothing. You think about it the whole ride home.
Gone in one bite. You ask what it was. The waiter says "an idea."

activities.title: The corner at sunset
activities.blurb: There's one corner where the sun drops right between two towers. Six people want it. There's room for one.

outcomes.text: The sun drops right between the towers. Your photo looks fake. People ask if it's fake. It's not.
A finance guy's vest gets into every single frame. It's the vest's sunset now.

options.label: Let a nervous couple have it

outcomes.text: The nervous guy proposes in your corner. She says yes. They want you in the wedding photos.
They take one photo and leave. The sun's gone. You photograph the dark. It's moody. It works.

activities.title: Watch the fireworks
activities.blurb: Thaddeus is renting railing space at C$30 a foot. The show starts in ten minutes and the roof is filling fast.

options.label: Rent a foot of railing
options.cost: C$30 for one foot of railing

outcomes.text: Your foot of railing is perfect. The first burst goes off right in front of you and the whole roof gasps.
You're behind a man holding his phone up the entire time. You watch the fireworks on his phone.

options.label: Watch from the back with the staff

outcomes.text: The busboys have a crate and a secret angle that beats the railing. They let you stay. They share fries.
Mostly smoke and the backs of heads. But the staff share their fries, and it's a good night.

happenings.title: Lunch rush
happenings.blurb: The line's out the door. Andreas could use a hand.

happenings.title: Greek night
happenings.blurb: Live bouzouki and a lot of plates. Fridays and Saturdays.

happenings.title: Candlelight story night
happenings.blurb: The power's out. Lola made it an event.

happenings.title: Morning rush
happenings.blurb: Thirty coffees, one Sal. He needs help.

happenings.title: Pre-work stampede
happenings.blurb: Every commuter in Astoria needs oat milk in ninety seconds. Jojo's on alone. Weekdays.

happenings.title: Rain refuge
happenings.blurb: Half of Astoria is waiting out the storm in here. Every seat's taken. Every rumor's out.

happenings.title: Golden Hour day party
happenings.blurb: Sunlight through warehouse windows, sunglasses indoors, a DJ who calls it "afternoon energy." Weekends.

happenings.title: Line around the block
happenings.blurb: The whole city wants out tonight. The line runs past the bodega and Mags needs hands behind the bar.

happenings.title: Pool hours
happenings.blurb: The public pool is open. The swim-cap lady is on duty. She will check.

happenings.title: Sprinkler day
happenings.blurb: Too hot to think, so the Parks guy opened the sprinklers and half of Astoria is standing in them.

happenings.title: Hard-hat lunch
happenings.blurb: Every construction worker on 31st Street wants two slices and a soda in the next eight minutes. Weekdays.

happenings.title: Stranded commuters
happenings.blurb: The trains stopped. Half of 31st Street is stuck under the el with nowhere to go but Arben's.

happenings.title: Friday tournament
happenings.blurb: Brackets on the big screen, a stage, a crowd and a trophy shaped like a controller. Pixel hosts.

happenings.title: Generator night
happenings.blurb: The power's out and the rigs are dark. Pixel's running one old TV off the backup generator.

happenings.title: Coach Bogdana's 6 AM
happenings.blurb: No music. Just her voice and the sound of people regretting it. Monday, Wednesday, Friday.

happenings.title: Sunset hour
happenings.blurb: The skyline turns gold and every phone on the roof goes up at once. Thaddeus dims the music out of respect.

happenings.title: Fireworks night
happenings.blurb: There's a festival on the waterfront and the roof has the best seat in Brooklyn. Thaddeus is charging for the railing.

moments.title: A tourist needs directions
moments.blurb: "Excuse me, which way to Times Square?" They're holding a paper map upside down and wearing a foam Statue of Liberty crown.

options.label: Walk them to the right train

outcomes.text: You get them on the right N train. They take a selfie with you. You're in a family album in Ohio now.
You get them on the right train going the wrong way. You find out an hour later. You tell no one.

options.label: Send them "the scenic way"
options.cost: A tiny bit of your soul

outcomes.text: You send them to a great slice place in Astoria instead. They post a review thanking "a local legend."
You send them to Staten Island. You feel bad for nine seconds.

moments.title: Hold my ring light?
moments.blurb: An influencer needs someone to hold their ring light "for literally one take." You can see forty takes in their eyes.

outcomes.text: Take 31 is the one. They tag you. Their 80,000 followers ask who the hot assistant is.
Take 46. They thank you and forget to tag you. Your arms will remember this.
"Wait, that's actually a good idea." You film it together. It does better than their solo stuff. Awkward.
"I'll have my team reach out." They do not have a team. Nobody will reach out.

moments.title: A hot tip
moments.blurb: A guy in a fleece vest leans over: "Not financial advice, but… are you in on Bodega Coin?"

outcomes.text: Buried in the nonsense is one real tip: the deli on 31st is hiring at double pay. You pocket it.
It's a coin with a cat on it. It was down 90% while he explained it. He's still bullish.
"Is the vest also not financial advice?" The table behind you loses it. He takes the vest off. Growth.
He laughs harder than anyone and asks you to co-host his podcast. You've made it worse.

moments.title: Take our picture?
moments.blurb: A family of six hands you a phone. "Get the bridge in. And all of us. And our shoes. We bought the shoes here."

outcomes.text: You crouch, tilt and get the bridge, six faces and the shoes. It's their holiday card now. You're credited.
Forty photos. The dad blinks in every one. On purpose, you realize. It's his thing.
You flip the camera by mistake and take nine photos of yourself. They keep one. "You have a good face for it."
They find the selfies at dinner. Their review of New York mentions you. Three stars.

moments.title: Be in my "get ready with me"?
moments.blurb: An influencer is filming and needs "a random New Yorker" to react to her outfit. You are, apparently, random.

outcomes.text: "The jacket's doing a lot. Too much. Keep it." She loves it. Your quote becomes the caption.
"Okay, we'll cut that." She cuts it. She cuts you. You were never there.
"Iconic. Who did your eyebrows?" She tags you. Her followers find you very supportive.
You hype so hard the comments ask if you're paid. You're not. You wish.

moments.title: A metal business card
moments.blurb: "Love your energy. Ever think about consulting?" He hands you a card. It's metal. It's heavy. It says "Visionary."

outcomes.text: You out-jargon him. "Let's take this offline." He pays you C$80 on the spot for "advisory." You advised nothing.
It's a pyramid. A very nice pyramid, with a mission statement. You leave before the second slide.

options.label: Scrape gum off your shoe with it

outcomes.text: It works perfectly. Best tool you've ever owned. He sees, and nods slowly. "That's disruption."
He sees. He's hurt. He hands you another card. This one says "Visionary (Forgiving)."

moments.title: Hold these six leashes?
moments.blurb: "Thirty seconds, I swear." A dog walker hands you six leashes and runs into the bodega. The dogs pick six directions.

outcomes.text: You hold the line. The dogs sit, impressed. The walker comes back and tips you C$20 and a biscuit.
Kevin the pug leads a coup. You're dragged half a block. The walker films it. You're "leash guy" now.

options.label: Sit down on the sidewalk with them

outcomes.text: Six dogs climb on you. A stranger says "thank you for this." You don't know what for. Same.
A doodle sits on your phone and posts a photo of the sky. It does better than your average post.

moments.title: Park-bench intel
moments.blurb: "You didn't hear it from me, but Sir Barksley has a new walker. Second one this month. Want to know why?"

outcomes.text: The new walker tried to put Sir Barksley on a juice cleanse. Lola is going to faint. You run to tell her.
The reason is "scheduling." That's it. That's the tea. It's decaf.
"Wow, okay, principled." They tell the whole park you're trustworthy. That's its own kind of clout.
They tell you anyway, louder. You'll tell no one. You'll think about it all week.

moments.title: Free medical advice
moments.blurb: A nurse fresh off twelve hours squints at you. "When did you last drink water? Real water. Not coffee."

outcomes.text: She buys you a water and watches you drink all of it. You feel ten years younger.
She sighs the sigh of someone who has seen everything. "Tuesday. Of course."
She almost believes you. Then she sees your lips. "Liar." She buys you two waters.
"Your lips say Tuesday." She hands you a water and writes HYDRATE on a napkin. You keep the napkin.

moments.title: Who's buying?
moments.blurb: Two night-shift workers argue about who bought the last coffee. Neither remembers. Both are too tired. Both look at you.

outcomes.text: Two coffees, two worst-shift stories. You're friends now, the tired kind.
They both fall asleep before the coffee arrives. You drink all three. You're vibrating.

options.label: Settle it with a coin toss

outcomes.text: Heads. The nurse wins. The rider pays and says "best two out of three" for the rest of the night.
The coin rolls under the counter. Everyone stares at it. Nobody has the energy. They split it.

moments.title: Need a duo partner
moments.blurb: "My duo partner just rage-quit. Out loud. In front of his mom. You play?"

outcomes.text: You don't know the game. You win anyway. He calls you "a natural" on stream. Fourteen viewers saw it.
You walk into a wall for four minutes. He mutes you. Chat calls you "the wall guy." It's catching on.
He wins with you yelling "GO" at every moment and insists you were the reason. You were not.
He loses and blames the cheering. Fair. You were yelling "go" at a loading screen.

moments.title: Try my app?
moments.blurb: "You build a startup. Inside the startup, you build a game. It's games all the way down." They hold out a phone.

options.label: Test it seriously
options.cost: Twenty minutes of a buggy app

outcomes.text: You find six bugs and one feature. They put you in the credits as "Chief Vibes Officer."
It crashes on launch. Four times. They call that "the beta experience."
They take it and hand you a sticker that says INVESTOR. The sticker is great. The sticker may be the asset.
"We're pre-revenue, so cash is weird for us." They decline and give you a sticker anyway.

moments.title: Is this your order?
moments.blurb: A rider holds up a bag. "Order for… Chazz? It says this building." You are not Chazz. Nobody here is Chazz.

outcomes.text: You find Chazz on a fire escape. Chazz tips big. The rider splits it with you.
There is no Chazz. There never was. The rider says this happens every week. You share a moment.
Forty minutes on the stoop. You learn his whole route and his mom's soup recipe. Chazz never shows.
Chazz walks up, takes the bag and says "you two look close." You are, now.

moments.title: Chain's off
moments.blurb: A rider's chain just came off in front of you. Four orders going cold and a look like the whole city owes him.

outcomes.text: Chain's back on in two minutes. He hands you a dumpling from "an order that was going to be late anyway."
You put it on backwards. Somehow it works better. He's confused but grateful.

options.label: Hold the bags while he fixes it

outcomes.text: He fixes it, thanks you and tells every rider on 31st you're good people. Free word of mouth.
A customer walks up, takes their food straight from you and tips you. You split it with him, honorably.

moments.title: Run lines with me?
moments.blurb: "My audition is in an hour for Woman Who Screams at Pigeon Number Two. Read the pigeon. Please. I need a pigeon."

outcomes.text: You coo with your whole chest. Strangers stop. A man claps. They get the part and thank "my pigeon" online.
Your pigeon is too good. They say you upstaged them. As a pigeon. You both get a little emotional.
"Try it angrier at the pigeon." Perfect. They get the callback and credit you loudly.
"I didn't ask for notes, I asked for a pigeon." Fair. They go find another pigeon.

moments.title: A sudden musical number
moments.blurb: Someone starts singing at you. It's a song about rent. They're looking at you to take the harmony.

outcomes.text: Your harmony lands. The whole room joins the chorus about rent. Somebody films it and it travels.
You find a harmony nobody has ever heard. Not a good one. They keep singing, braver than anyone.

options.label: Clap on one and three
options.cost: Everyone hears you clap on one and three

outcomes.text: They forgive the clapping and take a bow. You take a smaller bow. It feels right.
A man beside you says "two and four" firmly. You learn something today.

moments.title: Back in my day
moments.blurb: "This used to be a bakery. Then a bank. Then a bakery again. Now it's an oat milk place. Sit, I'll explain."

outcomes.text: The 1977 blackout, on this exact block. Better than any podcast. He makes you promise to remember it.
The story becomes about his knee. Then his other knee. Both knees have excellent stories.

options.label: Ask for the best food on the block

outcomes.text: He writes it on a napkin: "Arben's, the corner slice. Tell him Yiannis sent you." You're in.
"Everything's terrible now." A pause. "Except the deli. And the bakery. And the cart." It's a long list.

moments.title: A dollar a game
moments.blurb: "I've played here since 1971. I've lost eleven times. Want to be number twelve?"

options.label: Play, for real
options.cost: A dollar a game, your pride

outcomes.text: Checkmate in thirty moves. He laughs and adds your name to a list in his pocket. You're number twelve.
He beats you in nine moves while eating a sandwich. "Come back tomorrow. You're getting worse."
He destroys a finance guy in six moves and explains every one to you. Better than a semester.
His next opponent is a pigeon. Not chess, exactly. You're not sure who's winning.

moments.title: Be my co-founder?
moments.blurb: "It's a dating app, but for co-founders. I need a co-founder to build it. You look free."

outcomes.text: You sketch it on a napkin. It's actually good. You both agree to "circle back." Great napkin, though.
Your role is "everything except the idea." The idea is a website. You resign in nine minutes.
He loves it so much he gets visibly nervous. "Let's not talk numbers here." You've won.
He writes it down, badly. You watch him misunderstand your idea into a worse one. It's freeing.

moments.title: Rate my morning routine
moments.blurb: "Four AM cold plunge, journaling at 4:15, mushroom coffee at 4:30, then a meeting with myself. Thoughts?"

outcomes.text: He lights up and follows you everywhere. Online. You get a thank-you message at 4:15 AM.
He invites you to join tomorrow at four. You agree, panic and set eleven alarms.
A long silence. "Seven." He tries it. Next week he looks ten years younger and credits "a stranger."
"Sleep is a mindset." He leaves to go be awake somewhere else.

moments.title: Sit for a sketch?
moments.blurb: An art student holds up a sketchbook. "Can I draw you? You have a very specific face. That's a compliment. Mostly."

outcomes.text: It's beautiful and slightly too honest about your nose. They post it. People say "that's so them."
They draw you as a pigeon. "It's how I see you." You're not sure how to feel. You kind of love it.
Your drawing is a stick figure with great hair. They frame it. "Raw. Outsider. Honest."
They look at your drawing for a long time. "Do you want to talk about it?"

moments.title: Come to my show?
moments.blurb: "It's my thesis show. It's in a laundromat. The theme is 'spin cycle.' There's wine in paper cups."

options.label: Go, and buy a piece
options.cost: C$40 for a sock on a canvas

outcomes.text: You buy the sock. The artist tears up. Three people ask who the collector is. You are, now.
You buy the sock, then it goes through a dryer by accident. The artist calls it "the final form."
Your review calls it "a wash, in the best way." It goes on the laundromat wall. People quote you.
You forget. They remind you daily for a week. You write "good show" and it's somehow worse.

moments.title: Watch the stroller?
moments.blurb: "Two seconds, I'm grabbing his juice." A nanny parks a stroller beside you. The baby stares at you like a landlord.

outcomes.text: He laughs so hard he hiccups. The nanny comes back and says you're hired. She's joking. Mostly.
The baby does not laugh. The baby judges. It feels like a job interview you failed.
You guard it like a museum guard guards a painting. The nanny gives you a nod that says "you get it."
The baby throws a sock. You catch it, one hand, clean. A man across the street applauds.

moments.title: Playground politics
moments.blurb: "The Tuesday nannies and the Thursday nannies aren't speaking. You're new. Pick a side, sweetie, and pick it fast."

outcomes.text: Tuesday adopts you. You learn which building's doorman is secretly dating which super.
Thursday finds out in eleven minutes. The sandbox goes quiet when you walk in.
Both sides respect it. Neither tells you anything ever again. Neutral is lonely.
They make you referee the sandbox dispute. You rule for a toddler. Everyone accepts it.

feta-compli.text: Andreas remembers your name. Mostly. "My friend!"
Family table: Andreas sits you at the good table by the window.
His mother's lamb, not on the menu, saved for you on Fridays.

neon-spoon.text: Lola learns your name and starts mispronouncing it on purpose.
Your initials on the regulars' wall, next to a dog nobody remembers.
Lola saves you a booth during every Tea drop. You're inner circle.

ditmars-deli.text: Sal starts your order when you walk in. You didn't tell him what it was.
Meatball the cat tolerates you. This is unprecedented.
Your sandwich goes on the board: "The Regular." Sal denies naming it after you.

grind-and-gossip.text: Jojo spells your name right. Once. As a warning.
Your drink goes on the chalkboard as "The Usual (Don't Ask)."
Jojo tells you the gossip before it happens. The tip jar is still for film school.

velvet-static.text: Mags knows your drink. She makes it before you ask, and judges it.
The bouncer nods at you. Not a smile. A nod. That's the whole VIP.
Mags lets you pick the last song of the night. Choose wisely.

hell-gate-park.text: Gus saves you the end of the bench. You have to hear about 1987, but still.
Sir Barksley wags once when you arrive. Dmitri wrote it down.
Gus teaches you his backgammon opening. He hasn't shown anyone since 1974.

still-a-dollar-slice.text: Arben folds your slice before you can. It's an honor and also kind of a lot.
You get the corner slice. Nobody gets the corner slice.
A dollar, spiritually and actually: Arben charges you the sign price. Once.

respawn-arena.text: Pixel learns your gamer tag and says it with total respect.
A good chair. Not the Arcade Nerds' chairs, but a good chair.
Your name on the wall of champions, in Pixel's best marker.

pressed-iron-gym.text: The front desk stops asking your name. They've written it down. Somewhere.
Coach Bogdana says "not bad." Out loud. In front of people.
Your own locker and your name on the chalk wall of PRs. Spelled right.

altitude-718.text: Thaddeus finds your name on the list without looking. It's a trick. It still works.
The edge table, no waitlist. Thaddeus calls it "a cancellation." Every time.
The chef sends out a tiny plate with your name on it. It's still one bite.
